text.content:
The city was not originally a High Elven colony like many of the other Tilean city-states and grew up in a rambling way over many centuries. Its princes have gradually imposed an orderly plan on the city. This was initially drafted by the great Leonardo da Miragliano who was commissioned with this task by Prince Cosimo. It has taken many centuries since then to bring the plan to fruition. Each subsequent prince and many of the merchant families have endeavoured to beautify the city with palazzi, piazzas, fine bridges and sculptures.

Archaic Age (ca. -700 to -1 IC)

  • ca. -15 IC - A Tilean merchant from Miragliano discovers the River of Echoes, a ribbon of dark water that passes beneath the Vaults and into the heartland. The expedition wonders north and builds a fortified trading post on High Elven ruins. The settlement is called Nuln and quickly becomes a rallying point for local tribes in times of trouble. Tilean traders spread the worship of their Classical Gods, especially Shallya, and Verena.

Era of the Araby Wars (1240 to 1491 IC)

  • 1382 to 1420 IC - A series of indecisive conflicts arises between Bretonnian barons and mercenaries in the pay of the Prince of Miragliano. The skirmishes take place in the foothills of the Iranna Mountains, near the small town of Ravola which is famed for its vineyards.

  • 1425 IC - The Prince of Miragliano arranges a conference to put a stop to the feuding between Tilean landowners and Bretonnian barons. The Bretonnian Baron du Bors challenges the Tilean venator Etto ‘The Fierce' to a joust. The resulting Tournament of Ravola sees the flower of Bretonnian chivalry soundly beaten by Tilean knights and ends Bretonnian pretensions to domains in Tilea.

Age of Exploration (1492 to 1999 IC)

  • ca. 1600 IC - Caccino the Wise, priest of great renown in the Cult of Verena, establish a great temple of the goddess deep below the folds of the Irrana Mountains in northern Tilea.

  • 1711 IC - Grand Count Maximilian III von Hochkirsche, Elector of Nuln, loose his last battle against the mercenary forces of Miragliano, thus abandoning any claim towards the principality.

  • 1812 IC - The Red Pox spread in northern Tilea from Bretonnia. In Miragliano, nearly one in three citizens is laid low by the disease. Large rats are blamed for spreading the pox, and Miragliano begins to employ a standing force of Rat Catchers among their mercenary troops. Skaven armies emerged in the wake of the pox, expecting to find Bretonnia and Tilea weaker targets than the Empire. However, the people of both countries put up a desperate defence, and the Skaven force was defeated.

  • ca. 1999 IC - A small area in downtown Miragliano is overrun by vermin. All of the citizens have fled or died in these disease-ridden streets and the Governor Maximo anxious to rid the city of the vile and diseased terror before it spreads to other districts throughout the city hires many different warbands as ratcatchers with the perspective of a rich reward, five gold crowns for every full bag of rats.

Era of Enlightenment (2000 IC to Present)

  • 2000 IC - A new age of art, culture, and prosperity flourishes in Tilea. In Miragliano, a city that had developed in a rambling way over many centuries, a bold redevelopment plan is implemented by Prince Cosimo. He employs Leonardo da Miragliano to redesign the city's streets and plazas. Leonardo builds many towers that list in the marshy ground. Rather than being regarded as a liability, the towers spark a fashion of leaning structures that goes on to characterise many of Tilea's cities.

  • 2004 IC - The Skaven siege the city of Miragliano and are driven back, Leonardo da Miragliano took part to the battle and analyzed the Skaven machinery such as the Screaming Bell.

  • 2192 IC - Duke Alfonzo of Miragliano mounted a massive offense into the Zombie Swamps in a conflict known as the Battle of the Blight while suffering heavy casualties the Tileans managed to push back the Skavens deeper into the Blighted Marshes and expelled the Ratmen from the areas surrounding Miragliano this allowed principality to expand into territory that was previously uninhabitable thanks to the Skavens.

  • 2235 IC - The explorer Guido Pasolini mounts an expedition to the source of the Cristallo River, only to discover that the ancient legend of the River of Echoes is true. The discovery brings great power to the city of Miragliano. With time Miragliano and Remas, have taken advantage of the discovery of the River of Echoes from northern Tilea to Wissenland to set up trading offices in Nuln, Pfeildorf, and other southern towns. Hoping to use this as a reliable route to bypass Marienburg and cut costs since the mountain passes are frequently blocked by snow.

  • 2243 IC - The pirate captain known as the Black Cygnet returns from plundering shipping lanes to the New World. He uses his ill-gotten gains to establish the estate of Udolpho. Rumours begin to circulate that it is a site of dark and experimental sorcery.

  • 2276 IC - A Bretonnian army crosses northern Tilea territory to gain access to the Old Dwarf Pass to lend its help to the Border Princes raided by Settra's Undead hordes. Supported by a great number of mercenaries, Sir Cecil Gastonne and other Bretonnian exiled knights muster their forces and marched on the Principality of Matorea to meet their enemies in a decisive battle.

  • 2283 IC - Smarra Udolpho invites the household of Isabelle Di Lambrusco to visit the Udolpho estate to celebrate their impending nuptials. Isabelle's jealous brother murders her on the eve of the wedding. She returns from the grave to haunt the estate as the Spectre Bride.

  • ca. 2302 IC - After the defeat of the Witch King Malekith in Ulthuan at the Battle of Finuval Plain, Asarnil begin his self-exile with Deathfang in the city of Remas and is hired by the Prince of the city-state against Miragliano. In the naval battle of the Siren‘s Rocks, Asarnil and Deathfang destroyed Miragliano‘s entire fleet, and ended the city‘s supremacy at sea.

  • 2302-2320 IC - Terror in Tilea. In the years that follow the Great Summoning, a number of attacks are made on the Tilean city-states. Many small towns bordering on the Blighted Marshes are razed or simply disappeared.

  • 2309 IC - During the summer, the Imperial scholar Wilhelm Leiber visits Miragliano. With great stupor, he discovers that Tileans don't deny the existence of the Skaven and to the contrary are eager to share their knowledge on the matter and seek new allies against their menace. Once back in his homeland, the man wrote his magnum opus, The Loathsome Ratmen and All Their Vile Kin, to alert the Empire about the incoming danger, but his book was destroyed by the church of Altdorf and Wilhelm spent his last days in an asylum.

  • 2321 IC - Skaven warships are spotted in the Tilean Sea. Many coastal raids begin at this time. During the winter, Clan Eshin Gutter Runners make a number of raids on Imperial, Bretonnian, Tilean and Estalian warfleets at anchor in their respective ports. The Gutter Runners use firepots and naptha to burn the fleets with varying levels of success. In the end the Dwarfs of Barak-Varr destroyed the Skaven fleet. To date the perpetrators of these attacks are still unknown to the Tileans which only have seen flotillas of strange ramshackle craft near Tobaro.

  • 2418 IC - Otranto Udolpho, a maverick sorcerer, tried to conquer the Udolpho estate at the head of an army consisting of Undead troops and a regiment of Daemonettes.

  • 2430 IC - Melmoth Udolpho sells his soul to Slaanesh in return for a promise that he would never be bored again.

  • 2442 IC - The Miraglianese sculptor Angelo Fittorini becomes renowned for his beautiful depictions of the gods and goddesses of the Old World.

  • 2460 IC - The construction of Heinrich Kemmler's fortress, Krinal, within the the Vaults is completed, from where the necromancer will terrorise the northern lands of Tilea.

  • ca. 2460 to 2470 IC - Kemmler's growing ambitions eventually bring him into conflict with Khemalla of Lahmia, a Vampire of the Lahmian bloodline who had established a lair in Miragliano. Seeking dark knowledge, Kemmler attacked her lair and pillaged her library, forcing Khemalla to flee both her den and the Tilean city-state.

  • 2470 IC - The princes of several Tilean cities secretly pledged allegiance to Kemmler in order to spare themselves the worst of his raids. The necromancer instead turned his attention towards the Bretonnian province of Carcassonne.

  • 2479 IC - Kemmler was cast out from his fortress at Krinal and moved even deeper into the Vaults.

  • 2485 IC - Borgio the Besieger made himself Prince of Miragliano. He proceeded to execute so many of his enemies by hanging them from Miragliano's leaning towers that the buildings are said to lean more during his reign than at any other time.

  • ca. 2485 IC - The Reman general Mandalari the Magnificent siege the city of Miragliano. Thanks to a stratagem plotted by Prince Borgio, the Miraglianese army manages to disrupt the attack, routed by the timely counter-assault the Reman host is forced to flee.

  • 2489 IC - At the battle of Villa Vennia, Borgio the Besieger defeats a mercenary army from the Republic of Remas.

  • 2495 IC - Battle of Via Veddia, Miragliano defeats Verezzo.

  • 2497 IC - Donato brokes an alliance with Trantio but perishes after consuming a meal of poisonous mushrooms. His widow, Lucrezzia Belladonna, soon remarries, choosing the dashing captain Ranuccio for her husband. At the battle of Vittoria Viccia, Borgio the Besieger defeats a mercenary army from the Principality of Trantio, assisted by the last minute betrayal of the mercenaries from Pavona who attack their Trantine allies in the rear. Miragliano is established as the most powerful principality in Tilea.

  • 2503 IC - Borgio the Besieger is murdered in his bath with a toasting fork. Street fighting breaks out in Miragliano as various factions vie for power, and Borgio's excellent mercenary army fragments as captains lead their regiments away from the city in the hope of new employment. Braganza's Besiegers, Vespero's Vendetta, and Bronzino's Galloper Guns are just a few of these regiments of renown.

  • 2506 IC - Ysidro d'Amato, styling himself ‘The Water Wizard', becomes one of the richest merchants in Miragliano after monopolising the city's supplies of potable water.

  • 2507 IC - Miragliano is beset by a virulent outbreak of the Yellow Ague, which is traced back to the water sold by d'Amato. Calls for his arrest are made but he flees the city and vanishes. Genevieve Dieudonné manage to escape with Aleksandr Kloszowski and Antonia Marsillach from the haunted estate of Udolpho.

Miragliano, officially the Mighty Principality of Miragliano and also known as "Miragliano the Serene", is one of the most powerful city-states in Tilea, famed for its expert crossbowmen. Miragliano stands as a bastion of Human defiance against the Skaven hordes of the Under-Empire, whose capital, Skavenblight, lies just to the west of the city beneath the treacherous Blighted Marshes.

The city itself rests upon hundreds of small islands connected by stone-banked canals. While the landward side is marshy and unpleasant, Miragliano itself is remarkably airy, clean, and well-ordered, a stark contrast to the chaotic, labyrinthine imperial cities of the Old World. Under the direction of the genius @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#leonardo-da-miragliano]{Leonardo da Miragliano}, Prince Cosimo once leveled much of the old city to build a meticulously planned metropolis. The city is organized into distinct, identifiable districts. The safer inland areas house the wealthy merchant princes, artistically enriched temple quarters, and showcase the city's immense wealth and devotion. The outer sections are entrusted to mercenary barracks, bustling taverns, brothels, and the hard-working sailors and laborers who fill the princes' coffers.

As a premier trading hub, Miragliano boasts Tilea's largest fleet. Its small, light ships regularly sail as far as the deep south, despite having to run the blockade of Magrittan ships in the Southern Sea. The docks of Miragliano host a vibrant tapestry of merchants from Marienburg, the Empire, Araby, and even the near-mythical Elf realm of Ulthuan. Likewise, ambitious Miraglianian traders can be found throughout the Old World, buying furs, sea ivory, and amber in Erengrad, trading New World goods in Marienburg, or bartering in Magritta. This ambitious spirit extends to their social structures: while all Old World cities have guilds, in Miragliano they function more like anarchic "clubs", a far cry from the strictly controlled systems of Talabheim or Marienburg.

Life in the Serene Principality revolves around its waters, though fresh water remains a precious commodity. The surrounding sea is undrinkable and the northern marsh streams lie miles away, forcing residents to buy drinking water from sellers who ply the canals in small barges. These broad, elegant waterways serve as streets, filled with continuous traffic of ornate barges passing under numerous bridges. However, the canals can grow foul and make the city vulnerable to plagues and clandestine Skaven agents. To counter this threat, canal gates blocked by massive iron portcullises are vigilantly guarded by rat-catchers.

The defenses of Miragliano are formidable, engineered by Leonardo da Miragliano and later refined by @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#borgio-the-besieger]{Prince Borgio}. The city features a very wide moat and walls specially designed to give maximum advantage to defensive artillery. Rising above the soggy foundations are numerous tall watchtowers built to command views far across the flat landscape. Unstable ground has caused most of these towers to lean at awkward angles, yet thanks to exceptional engineering skills, they remain standing. This quirk set an architectural fashion copied across Tilea, especially in Luccini, so that every city now boasts or aspires to have a leaning tower of its own. Prince Borgio the Besieger once dryly noted that executed men looked so much better hanging from a leaning tower, and during his rule, hanging opponents a dozen at a time was said to tilt the structures a couple more degrees!

As traditional patrons of learning, science, and warfare, the Princes of Miragliano have fostered an environment where minds like Leonardo and Borgio began their careers. Today, Miragliano remains a key destination for imperial engineers, who journey here on study voyages to learn from the most refined minds amid the classic grandeur of Tilea.

Alfonzo of Miragliano

Duke Alfonzo of Miragliano was the commander of the mercenaries which liberated in a huge expedition the Zombie Swamps and the lands around Miragliano from the Skavens.

Borgio the Besieger

Borgio was Prince of Miragliano, nicknamed “The Besieger” because of his unsurpassed expertise in siege warfare.

Cornuti

The Cornuti are the most powerful family of Miragliano.

Dolchellata Belladonna

Dolchellata Belladonna is the widow of Borgio and older sister of Lucrezzia Belladonna.

Countess Carlotta de Villarias

Countess Carlotta de Villarias is a young and eccentric Estalian noblewoman, in addition to possessing a timeless beauty that has been shaped throughout time by artists.

Ennio Corbucci Volonte

Ennio Corbucci Volonte was once a powerfull and feared loan shark from Miragliano. Whose only daughter is married to Alberto Bertolucci.

Leonardo da Miragliano

Leonardo da Miragliano was one of the greatest inventors ever born in the Old World.

Verspasian Kant

Verspasian Kant is the present day Magister Patriarch of the White Order of Altdorf.

Ysidro d'Amato

A water merchant known in all Miragliano as the Water Wizard. He made fortune via water-caravans and canals, carving out his own empire, forcing his competitors out of business and building a monopoly. When the Yellow Ague came, and investigating scryers laid the blame on contaminated water, Ysidro left the city.

The more prosperous districts of Miragliano sit right at the heart of the old city, sheltered from the surrounding sprawl by a thick stone wall. The inner district rests on an island, physically separated from the maze of warehouses, shops, and taverns that cater to merchant fleets and their crews.

Access through the inner wall is controlled at a small pier running alongside a massive shutter. Here, entry is strictly guarded by @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#borgio-the-besieger]{Prince Borgio}’s elite troops rather than the mercenary guards hired by local merchant corporations. These men are hard-faced, scarred veterans who cut their teeth in ruthless warfare. Over their reinforced leather armor, each soldier wears a tabard displaying the scarlet field and black tower of the prince. Rat paws hang from the leather straps on their belts, serving as a grim reminder that exterminating Skaven threats and guarding the gates are part of their daily duties.

Beyond the gates, narrow canals and paved streets are lined with imposing palazzos. These grand residences feature tall, multi-story architecture with massive skylights and vibrant stained-glass windows, a decorative style even more prominent here than in the famous @UUID[Compendium.artantares-tilea.journals.JournalEntry.BhZS96hSdSN9addg.JournalEntryPage.28kZ3obbQ6WavhFt]{Ponte Eterno} of Remas.

The last line of defense of the city, should the enemy breach the other components of the fortification system, the citadel of Miragliano is defended by a gate enhanced by dwarf runes that burn bright red when operating.

Reachable by gondola, the cold and clammy palazzo of @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#countess-carlotta-de-villarias]{Countess Carlotta de Villarias} stands in Miragliano's most prosperous districts. Situated right in the heart of the old city, the palace rests on its own secluded island, protected from the surrounding sprawl of warehouses, shops, and taverns by a thick stone wall.

The estate itself is a massive gray stone building featuring an extravagant portico supported by fluted columns of black marble. Intricate stone carvings twist along the façade, evoking images of writhing snakes as much as trailing vines.

Inside, winding corridors and grand stairways are adorned with ancient marble statues resting on high pedestals. Between the statues hang portraits of once-powerful men, their features slowly fading with age. Each painting is the work of a distinct master, depicting noblemen dressed in the fashions of bygone eras. It is a singular collection, clearly bearing no familial connection to the mistress of the house.

Despite the fine artwork and elaborately engraved door frames, an unmistakable air of decay permeates the palazzo. Dust silently gathers in the corners, along the cracks of the marble floors, on the picture frames, and across the brows of the statues. Cobwebs hang from the high, vaulted ceilings, revealing that the Countess does not maintain a large household staff.

At the end of the main hallway, a pair of double doors made of dark Drakwald timber and carved with leering gargoyles leads into the Black Room. Inside, a floor of polished onyx stone shines beneath the flickering light of a hanging chandelier, while the walls remain entirely draped in heavy black cloth.

The fabulously wealthy Baroness Theodora Margrave is known as a noble native of Altdorf but in truth, she's a proud member of the Lahmian Sisterhood from Nuln. She is a patron of the arts. Particularly musicians and singers, and all of her servants can sing or play to delight her hosts.

Strada dei Cento Peccati (Street of the Hundred Sins) is a street near the port, full of taverns, brothels, premises dedicated to the witch's root, fighting pits and other places for even less decorous amusement. It is said that not even the most austere priest of Morr could cross that street without discovering something that would make him forget his priestly vows.

This street of illegal pleasures is the most dangerous in the whole city. It is a lawless district, to which even the guard dared not to venture during the night hours. Murder is more common than venereal disease and alcoholism, and not a single night goes by without a cart of corpses being collected the next morning from the quicklime pits outside the city. It is whispered that many more die without their bodies being found, either killed during dark rites, or abducted to be taken to the dwellings of necromancers. It is also rumored that some of the taverns and brothels, and especially the premises dedicated to the witch root, drug their customers, and that the unfortunate victims wake up in the secret cellars of some boat sailing towards distant slave markets, a fate perhaps worse than death.

The Purple Kitten

A bordello of the Strada dei Cento Peccati built on two floors is managed by Madame Livia, a wizened hag which would smite her girls to entertain some of the brothel's more curious customers, and their less than common tastes. Normally, the least appealing of the girls was given such duties, but Madame Livia never failed to threaten her prettier workers with such punishment when they were not compliant with her wishes and the demands of business.

The Black Boar

The Black Boar is a beer hall operated by a displaced Reiklander brewer, and catered especially to the needs of men from the Empire. The ceiling of the building is much higher than normal, for the floor was set well below street level. A sign in the shape of a dark and stout pig creature spells in crude letters, the name of the place written in Reikspiel. It is a brewery that offers alcoholic beverages more adapted to the particular tastes of the people who are looking for something stronger than Tilean wines and smooth Bretonnian beers. Mercenaries, sailors and caravan guards mainly from the Empire come here, although there are also Kislevites and some Dwarfs. To its patrons, it is a familiar setting in a foreign land.The Black Boar's patrons considered the inn a home away from home and viewed any Tilean who entered the tavern as an intruder.

The Maid of Albion

The Maid of Albion is a dockside tavern located in the seediest district of Miragliano. It is characterized by its burrow-like interior, a filthy environment befitting its reputation as a dive. The tavern serves as a gathering place for various unsavory characters, including seamen, mercenaries, and bandits, who frequent it to share their tales and drown their sorrows.

Sell-Sword Inn

An Inn requented mainly by mercenaries in search for a contract.

Merry Archer

An inn where the notorious Maximilian Damark, captain of the Marksmen of Miragliano enlist his new recruits, usually after noon.

Crooked Crossbow

An inn where the Marksmen of Miragliano hire youngbloods.

Purple Sheep

An inn frequented by both the common people and noblemen, such as the vengeful Peacocks. Here the clients often indulge in the pleasure of gambling.

A street infamous for its thriving black market, where illicit trade flourishes far from the watchful eyes of the law. Here, buyers can acquire illegal goods ranging from slaves kidnapped in the Strada dei Cento Peccati or other illegal weres.

Among the most sought-after substances is Crimson Shade, an addictive exotic drug used by Tileans seeking a lethal edge during personal vendettas and duels. The substance is also heavily consumed by the mercenary soldiers in the pay of the Prince of Miragliano. Unscrupulous merchants like Abdul-Qaadir amass vast fortunes by exploiting the powerful addiction created by this illegal trade.
Here is located the Quinsberry Lodge, an organisation dedicated to ensuring equal rights for Halflings across the Old World.
Power structure of the rulers of Miragliano, in its library are stored @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#leonardo-da-miragliano]{Leonardo}'s manuscripts.

Università di Miragliano (University of Miragliano) is an ancient and influential institution whose scholars range in the most disparate disciplines, from medicine to the study of the undead. The institute independently publishes its own texts thanks to the University of Miragliano Press, which over the centuries has published daring treatises, such as "Children of the Night: The Fall of the Von Carsteins" and the "Nature of Those They Command", printed in 2406 from Maria Conte's studies.

The Schola Chirurgica (Surgical School), is a place of science where medicine is studied in its various forms. Such it's its prestige that people from all over the Old World came to the University of Miragliano to study the wonders of modern medicine.

Miragliano foundries are known throughout the Old World for the production of the famous Miraglianese armours, even adopted by the Knightly Orders of the Empire. But the forges also churn out cannons such as those of the master gunner, Bronzino, renowned for the results they achieved during @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#borgio-the-besieger]{Borgio}'s expansion wars. Ironically, in the past the same forge used for the production of these weapons had been used by @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#leonardo-da-miragliano]{Leonardo da Miragliano} himself, for the production of his bronze statues.

The easternmost district remains a part of the old city that was never reconstructed. Five hundred years after the renovations of @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#leonardo-da-miragliano]{Leonardo da Miragliano}, it endures as a confusing, dilapidated maze of streets lying in complete abandonment. The land here is sinking, and the entire island is slowly crumbling into the surrounding marshes. The canals are choked with mud and weeds, making them completely unnavigable and forcing travelers to rely on a network of dubiously maintained bridges. Only the surrounding outer walls are preserved, shored up at their bases with boulders, rocks, and rubble to protect the city's overall defense line.

Few people venture into this deserted quarter. Laborers and scavengers occasionally navigate the broken cobblestones and rotting roofs to recover furniture, doors, or heavy stone statues from forlorn piazzas before the swamp consumes them. Otherwise, the district belongs only to those with something to hide. Even the local guard tower stands entirely unused.

In Tilea, the god of the sea is known as Mathann, and his cult plays a central role in the public life of Miragliano. Built upon the site of an ancient shrine, the current temple owes its existence to the maritime princes of the city and a generous donation from the Reman admiral Ludovico Dandola. While the faith in Tilea and Estalia lacks central unification, this grand chapel stands second in prominence only to the Great Cathedral in Marienburg and claims supreme authority across the southern Old World.

Reflecting its region, Mathann assumes a more classical character here than his northern counterpart in the Empire. The temple is a tall, colonnaded structure covered in vibrant frescoes depicting the Sea God alongside his numerous aquatic servants. Slender towers and elegant arches reveal an unmistakable Elven influence, portraying Mathann as the guardian of the placid Tilean Sea rather than the turbulent Sea of Claws.

Inside stands a statue of breathtaking beauty, carved by Leonardo da Miragliano from white marble shot through with turquoise veins. It depicts Mathann riding his chariot, pulled by dolphins and surrounded by graceful naiads and sea creatures. The masterpiece rests within a seawater pool that laps against the stone in gentle waves through an ingenious mechanical contrivance.

The local priesthood focuses heavily on protecting trade routes and countering the Stromfels-worshipping pirates of Sartosa. Although the clergy strives for neutrality in naval disputes with the rival city of Remas, local pride still breeds factionalism between the two temples. Leading the faith in Miragliano is High Priest Wave Lord Antonio Leontaris, a battle-hardened commander whose craggy face reflects decades of struggle against the corsairs of Sartosa and Araby. Under his command, a dedicated crew of captains investigates the emerging threat of the Skaven navies of Clan Skurvy and Clan Skuttle.

The Myrmidian temple of Miragliano was reduced to ruins by the Ratmen during the 26th century. To punish this wickedness, a group of mercenaries led by the Order of the Blazing Sun ventured into the stinking lairs of the skaven, far below the ruins of the temple. Among these adventurers there were also the famous duo made up of the Dwarf Slayer Gotrek and the Human chronicler Felix Jeager.
One of the main temples dedicated to Mercopio, the Lord of Commerce and Prosperity in the Old World, rivaling that of Marienburg and Magritta.

One of the largest Verenean Temple-Library. Such as every temple dedicated to Verena contains a library, crammed with every important tome that the local priests can acquire. It was here that a version of the story about the Tournament of Ravola was retrieved. The chronicle narrates of how thanks to the then Prince of Miragliano the Bretonnian claims on the lands of Tilea were stopped once and for all.

Surrounding Lands

Directly on the landward side of Miragliano stretch the vast, shallow Blighted Marshes, an unpleasant expanse of tall reeds and isolated patches of stable ground. Transport here relies entirely on barges, which enterprising water-sellers use to harvest freshwater for the thirsty city dwellers. To the west of the city lies the darkest section of these sinister swamps, housing Skavenblight, the capital of the Under-Empire. Because of this constant threat, the armies of Miragliano stand in perpetual readiness against Skaven incursions just as they do against rival city-states.

Beyond the marshes, the landscape shifts into fertile rolling hills, gentle meadows, fields of grain, orchards, vineyards, and pastures. This countryside forms the primary breadbasket of Miragliano, guarded by fortified outposts garrisoned by troops of Prince Borgio himself, who recognized that a hungry army wins no wars. Further northeast, where the stony soil becomes less hospitable, resilient locals cultivate olive trees, raise woolly mountain sheep, and grow fetore grapes for the region's signature frizzante wine.

Past the outermost forts, civilized farmland gives way to an ungoverned wilderness of rocky hills and deep, forested hollows. To the north lies a sandy plain dotted with scraggly thickets that encroach upon poorly maintained roads. This desolate region is inhabited only by hardened trappers, woodsmen, and rangers. Hardened bands of Beastmen and small tribes of Orcs and Goblins prowl the wilds, preying on merchant caravans. Human predators also haunt these lands, including outlaws and mercenaries who have deserted their companies. Wise travelers learn to distrust anyone encountered in these untamed hills.

Shrine of the Seven Mercies

Deep within the countryside surrounding Miragliano stands the Shrine of the Seven Mercies, where priestesses of Shallya attend to the poor peasants and farmers feeding the city. Behind its white walls and cross-shaped windows, the shrine features a classical marble altar portraying the goddess offering her golden heart to her worshippers as a symbol of selfless sacrifice.

Hidden beneath the altar's flagstones rests a dark glass bottle containing holy water from the High Temple in Couronne. These divine Tears of Shallya possess immense healing power, preserved by the order to protect the priestesses themselves from the deadly contagions they strive to cure. In recent times, the shrine survived a brutal siege by Nurgle-worshipping Warriors of Chaos during an outbreak of the Red Pox, saved only through the timely intervention of local militia and the bounty hunter Brunner.

Villa Bertolucci

Like many wealthy Tileans, the Bertolucci family maintains a retreat outside the city walls. Villa Bertolucci remains an imposing two-story structure, though time and abandonment have taken their toll. The grand upper level once housed bedchambers, music rooms, and dining halls, while the spacious ground floor contained servant quarters, kitchens, and stables. While the outer stone walls remain intact, the original wooden doors and shutters have rotted away, leaving shadowed rooms and neglected kitchens overgrown with weeds. To protect their investment, the House of Bertolucci pays mercenary bands to secure the ruin against roaming bandits and Beastmen.

Subsidiary Settlements

Miragliano functions as a regional center of power, holding significant political authority over numerous surrounding communities:

  • Alimento: A cavern-town that serves as a vital trade hub with the Empire.

  • Amato: A modest hamlet blessed by pure natural springs.

  • Campogrotta: A village under Miraglianese influence at the Tilean mouth of the Alimento Tunnel, home to a small community of Dwarfs.

  • Cammaro: A squalid village whose entire population mysteriously vanished in 2511 IC.

  • Ebino: An inland trading town under the political sphere of Miragliano.

  • Etobrutti: A poor rural hamlet.

  • Mironia: A squalid hamlet whose populace vanished in 2510 IC.

  • Parmis: A neglected village whose population vanished in 2512 IC.

  • Ravola: A bustling agricultural town renowned for producing the finest wines in Tilea.

  • Toscania: A small village featuring an established Dwarf trading post.

  • Udolpho: An average-sized hamlet widely avoided due to its reputation as a haunted estate.

  • Zeluco: A prosperous village famous for its formidable fortress and labyrinthine dungeons.

Foreign Settlements

Beyond the direct borders of the principality lie several independent strongholds that interact with Miraglianese trade and diplomacy:

  • Dragon Falls: An impregnable fortress situated where the Vaults meet the Irrana Mountains beyond Bretonnia's borders, garrisoned year-round by the Knights of Carcassonne.

  • Raganos: A high-altitude mining community in the Irrana Mountains famous for its lifelike warrior statues. It maintains functional independence by playing the rival Tilean city-states and Estalian kingdoms against one another.
Part of this neighborhood was burnt by the Estalian bright wizard, Sienna Fuegonasus during the collection of a debt.

Miragliano is renowned throughout the Old World for its master glassmakers, whose exquisite creations are crafted from pure quartz pebbles. Celebrated for their exceptional clarity and vivid colors, these vibrant glass panes are prized by major temples across the land to adorn their stained glass windows. So legendary is the skill of Miragliano's artisans that a glass crafted here is said to instantly shatter if a poisoned liquid is poured inside it.

Within the city, mirror-making is treated as a semi-mystical art, surrounded by religious reverence. Only the wealthiest and most privileged elites can afford to own one of these sublime reflective masterpieces.

Among these artisans, one of the most famous is Ilaria Acutis, a glassmaker obsessed with creating the absolute perfect mirrored surface. Striving for flawless silvering and unprecedented clarity, she experimented with exotic materials, eventually acquiring a small piece of warpstone smuggled out of nearby Skavenblight. The resulting mirror possessed unparalleled reflective qualities, but instead of portraying physical appearances, it altered the image to reflect the viewer's inner soul.

When word of the miraculous creation reached @UUID[.dx2P1MikfGnepapC#borgio-the-besieger]{Borgio the Besieger}, the prince demanded to purchase it. Upon gazing into the glass and seeing his soul revealed, an enraged Borgio ordered Acutis's execution, forcing the artisan to flee the city for Altdorf.
